This is a senior IT Operations role and is considered to be a SME (subject matter expert) in a specific domain such as Network, Security, or Infrastructure.

This role provides IT technical leadership across the primary technologies to the WCM community and is responsible for identifying incidents, events, and analyzing problem trends, overseeing the management and resolution of issues. Assists with data acquisitions, electronic discovery, and forensic investigations.
Works collaboratively with engineering team to provide continuing service management and support on all production and test/development systems. Provides support and maintenance for all current and new systems.

Develops knowledge base articles and work instructions for inclusion into knowledge base of record. Follows WCM ITIL process work flows to ensure operational tasks and activities are being followed for incident, request, change and event management.

Bachelor's Degree

Experience

Bachelor's degree in a related field, or five years of equivalent technical experience required.

ITIL v3 Foundations highly desired.

Advanced Linux, Microsoft, VMware, Network, Cisco, AWS, Azure, Security certification preferred.

Experience with LDAP, Active directory, DNS and DHCP technologies.

Experience with monitoring tools, various operating systems, backup, and cloud technologies.

Experience with PowerShell, Bash, Python, and Perl scripting.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Results driven individual who enjoys working in a fast paced and challenging environment.
Capable of working independently with little supervision or direction.
Excellent operations, troubleshooting, and critical thinking skills.
Technical acumen and the ability to facilitate and manage technical bridge lines that cross multiple domains.
Ability to quickly determine root cause, business impact and resolve issues as quickly as possible.

Licenses and Certifications

May participate in a rotation, providing 24x7x365 support.

Our purpose – Opening up a world of opportunity – explains why we exist. Here at HSBC, we use our unique expertise, capabilities, breadth, and perspectives to open up new kinds of opportunity for our more than 40 million customers. We’re bringing together the people, ideas and capital that nurture progress and growth, helping to create a better world – for our customers, our people, our investors, our communities, and the planet we all share.

In compliance with applicable laws, HSBC is committed to employing only those who are authorized to work in the US. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. as HSBC will not engage in immigration sponsorship for this position.

HSBC Americas is engaged in business in credit derivatives, emerging market and emerging market derivatives, mortgage, equity derivatives, fixed-income and interest rate derivatives, FX (Foreign Exchange), and commodities etc. Extensive risk models have been developed and well-documented to support these business activities. With Regulatory Stress Tests, methodology development and implementation, trading activities/strategies and risk management are more than ever driven by risk weighted return in the form of capital requirements, or risk weighted assets. At the meantime, risk engines are constantly being enhanced/consolidated to accommodate new regulations and anticipated changes. The mandate Risk Quantitative Analyst is to join the Global Risk Analytics team to research, develop and enhance traded risk methodologies, provide methodology support to regulatory stress test, businesses, traded risk management and control functions, interacting with regulatory agencies, and maintain and update the traded risk methodology documentation.

As Our Vice President Global Risk Analytics You Will

Review, validate and document risk methodologies across asset classes
Work on model assessment, monitoring tests, model performance and review and model risk governance. Responsible for conducting monthly model performance and review, investigating potential model performance issues and identifying areas for model enhancement
Manage the counterparty credit risk exposure for capital, limit and CVA (Credit Valuation Adjustment) calculation. According to regulatory standards to identify weaknesses and propose enhancements to satisfy all regulatory requirements and regulatory stress test)
Perform ad-hoc analysis in various aspects of risk measurements, stress tests, what-if analysis on the existing portfolios and during new product/transaction approval; and on demand quantitative support for businesses, and traded risk management and control functions
Work with the team to: develop advanced risk methodologies including sophisticated quantitative methodologies to measure counterparty credit and market risk exposures, and to enhance Value-at-Risk model, etc. Research and develop new risk methodologies to satisfy requirements of BASEL 3 and other regulatory frameworks. Research and develop methodology to address regulatory concerns and toward audit points removal

You´ll likely have the following qualifications to succeed in this role:

In depth knowledge on products and transactions in the various asset classes with solid understanding to their credit and market risk exposures and advanced quantitative methodologies to model and measure these risks. Strong working experience in quantitative financial methodologies (derivatives theory and models, probability theory, Mathematics, etc.) is required
Expertise in risk modeling development/enhancement. Demonstrated ability and experience in Regulatory Stress test, CVA, counteryparty credit risk and market risk models, and regulatory capital calculation
Excellent verbal and written skills. Must be able to explain and articulate complex quantitative and/or technical matters clearly, accurately and simply. Need interaction with US regulators, business heads, traders, quants, model review members, market risk and credit risk managers, and IT developers
Organized, detail-oriented and self-motivated, work independently, adhere to tight deadlines and develop and maintain healthy relationships with all internal clients and regulators
Solid technical skills are required, such as risk system/model implementation in Python, C/C++, VBA, or other programming languages. Knowledge on Traded/Risk Systems such as Polypaths, Calypso, Summit, etc. are plus
Advanced degree in a quantitative or computational field (Computer Science, Math, Physics, Statistics and Financial Engineering) is required

As an HSBC employee, you will have access to tailored professional development opportunities to ensure you have the right skills for today and tomorrow. We offer a competitive pay and benefits package including a robust Wellness Hub, all in a welcoming and inclusive work environment. You will be empowered to drive HSBC’s engagement with the communities we serve through an industry-leading volunteerism policy, a generous matching gift program, and a comprehensive program of immersive Sustainability and Climate Change Initiatives. You’ll want to join our Employee Resource Groups as they play a central part in life at HSBC, including the development of our employees and networking inside and outside of HSBC. Why this role is important to us

You will lead the technical execution of scenario-based testing against high-value systems and services, and you will own the validation of fixes for the resulting findings. Working with finding owners, offensive security partners, external testing providers, security operations, and risk and regulatory partners, you will make sure testing is realistic, findings are technically sound, and every fix holds up under real-world attack conditions. Serve as the senior technical lead across the engagement lifecycle, including scoping, test planning, rules of engagement, execution oversight, and post-test remediation planning.
Provide real-time technical guidance during engagements by assessing tester activity, judging operational risk, and guiding escalation decisions with appropriate discretion.
Hold external testing providers to a high technical standard by challenging their attack paths, evidence quality, severity ratings, and MITRE ATT&CK mapping, so that results are accurate, actionable, and defensible.
Lead coordination with finding owners and engineering teams to turn findings into clear technical remediation requirements and measurable validation criteria, so fixes address root causes rather than narrow point issues.
Lead the strategy for validating remediation. This includes grouping related findings, defining test criteria and expected outcomes, and personally retesting fixes against the original attack path and other ways of reaching the same objective.
Assess remediation across the wider estate, including variant attack paths, implementation consistency, and any new exposure the fix itself introduces.
Make the final technical call on closure recommendations, backed by evidence-based reporting that confirms each finding as closed, open, or partially closed, with executive summaries for senior and non-technical audiences.
Present testing and validation outcomes to senior leadership and governance forums, and defend the technical basis for findings, residual risk, and closure decisions.
Design and lead targeted TTP assessments and collaborative purple team exercises, so that detection, response, and preventive controls are validated against relevant attacker behavior.
Feed detection and control gaps found during testing to Detection Engineering, Assurance, and Security Operations, and track the resulting improvements through validation.
Provide offensive security support to partner teams, including risk and regulatory functions, and help set the methods, test plans, evidence standards, and lessons-learned practices that mature the internal capability. You will also mentor team members and partners.

Extensive hands-on experience in offensive security, such as advanced penetration testing, red teaming, or adversary simulation, ideally in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Expert-level practical knowledge of Active Directory and Entra ID attack paths, privilege escalation, lateral movement, credential abuse, EDR evasion, and cloud attack techniques across Azure and AWS.
Advanced proficiency with offensive tooling and C2 frameworks, such as Cobalt Strike, BloodHound, Mimikatz, Metasploit, and Kali Linux, plus scripting for custom tooling and automation (Python, PowerShell, or similar).
A proven record of leading remediation validation for complex findings, including defining closure criteria and deciding whether controls work in practice rather than just on paper.
Deep working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, scenario-based test design, and how detection and response capabilities are measured during testing.
Experience directing and challenging third-party testing providers, with the judgment to separate exploitable risk from theoretical findings.
Executive-level written and verbal communication, with the ability to defend technical conclusions to senior leadership, governance bodies, and independent reviewers.
Discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive, confidential engagement information.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Duties Description

The SIGNAL System Unit Coordinator (Business Systems Analyst 1 Health) serves as a full-performance business systems analyst for the Strategic Incident & Geospatial Notification, Analytics, and Logistics system, known as SIGNAL, the Division’s statewide emergency management information environment. The position works with the State Medical Operations Coordination Center, State EMS Task Force, Division emergency management programs, Department partners, health care facilities, EMS providers, local health departments, emergency management organizations, information technology staff, vendors, and other authorized system users. Work involving regulatory programs is limited to emergency management functions or information needed for preparedness and response and does not include administration of routine licensing, certification, investigation, or enforcement systems.

The position performs the full range of business systems analysis activities for multiple interrelated emergency management applications, workflows, data sets, reports, integrations, and user groups. Assignments require the coordinator to select and apply appropriate analytical techniques; evaluate current and proposed business processes; elicit and reconcile differing stakeholder requirements; translate emergency management needs into functional requirements, data specifications, workflows, reports, and acceptance criteria; and assess how proposed changes may affect downstream processes, notifications, data quality, access permissions, reporting, and system integrations. The coordinator independently completes assigned analyses and implementations within approved SIGNAL governance, configuration, security, documentation, and change-management standards and refers significant policy, system architecture, cybersecurity, contractual, or enterprise-priority matters to the SIGNAL System Unit Manager.

Errors in requirements, configuration, testing, data definitions, reporting, or implementation may result in incomplete or misleading situational awareness, delayed incident reporting or notifications, inaccurate facility, patient, or resource information, disrupted emergency management workflows, inappropriate access to sensitive information, or reduced system effectiveness during an incident. The work requires sound judgment to balance operational urgency, stakeholder needs, data quality, usability, information protection, continuity, technical feasibility, and long-term system sustainability, including during emergency activations when requirements and priorities may change rapidly. Emergency Management Business Process Analysis and Requirements Development

We are seeking a Vice President, Penetration Testing Analyst, to join State Street's Threat Intelligence and Assurance organization. This is a senior, hands-on technical role and serves as the team's in-house technical authority for complex penetration testing engagements and for validating remediation.

Why this role is important to us

You will lead the technical execution of scenario-based testing against high-value systems and services, and you will own the validation of fixes for the resulting findings. Working with finding owners, offensive security partners, external testing providers, security operations, and risk and regulatory partners, you will make sure testing is realistic, findings are technically sound, and every fix holds up under real-world attack conditions. You will be accountable for the technical defensibility of closure decisions presented to senior leadership and the Lines of Defense. You will also help mature a repeatable, high-quality internal testing capability.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As a Vice President, Penetration Testing Analyst, you will:

Serve as the senior technical lead across the engagement lifecycle, including scoping, test planning, rules of engagement, execution oversight, and post-test remediation planning.
Provide real-time technical guidance during engagements by assessing tester activity, judging operational risk, and guiding escalation decisions with appropriate discretion.
Hold external testing providers to a high technical standard by challenging their attack paths, evidence quality, severity ratings, and MITRE ATT&CK mapping, so that results are accurate, actionable, and defensible.
Lead coordination with finding owners and engineering teams to turn findings into clear technical remediation requirements and measurable validation criteria, so fixes address root causes rather than narrow point issues.
Lead the strategy for validating remediation. This includes grouping related findings, defining test criteria and expected outcomes, and personally retesting fixes against the original attack path and other ways of reaching the same objective.
Assess remediation across the wider estate, including variant attack paths, implementation consistency, and any new exposure the fix itself introduces.
Make the final technical call on closure recommendations, backed by evidence-based reporting that confirms each finding as closed, open, or partially closed, with executive summaries for senior and non-technical audiences.
Present testing and validation outcomes to senior leadership and governance forums, and defend the technical basis for findings, residual risk, and closure decisions.
Design and lead targeted TTP assessments and collaborative purple team exercises, so that detection, response, and preventive controls are validated against relevant attacker behavior.
Feed detection and control gaps found during testing to Detection Engineering, Assurance, and Security Operations, and track the resulting improvements through validation.
Provide offensive security support to partner teams, including risk and regulatory functions, and help set the methods, test plans, evidence standards, and lessons-learned practices that mature the internal capability. You will also mentor team members and partners.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Extensive hands-on experience in offensive security, such as advanced penetration testing, red teaming, or adversary simulation, ideally in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Expert-level practical knowledge of Active Directory and Entra ID attack paths, privilege escalation, lateral movement, credential abuse, EDR evasion, and cloud attack techniques across Azure and AWS.
Advanced proficiency with offensive tooling and C2 frameworks, such as Cobalt Strike, BloodHound, Mimikatz, Metasploit, and Kali Linux, plus scripting for custom tooling and automation (Python, PowerShell, or similar).
A proven record of leading remediation validation for complex findings, including defining closure criteria and deciding whether controls work in practice rather than just on paper.
Deep working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, scenario-based test design, and how detection and response capabilities are measured during testing.
Experience directing and challenging third-party testing providers, with the judgment to separate exploitable risk from theoretical findings.
Executive-level written and verbal communication, with the ability to defend technical conclusions to senior leadership, governance bodies, and independent reviewers.
Discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive, confidential engagement information.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10 or more years of related experience
Industry-recognized offensive security certifications such as OSCP, OSEP, OSCE3, CRTO, GXPN, or equivalent.
Experience supporting large-scale remediation validation programs is strongly preferred.
